issue.title: slows down any request in development mode

repository.name: activeadmin
repository.description: The administration framework for Ruby on Rails applications.

issue.body:
When having active admin with many models all requests in development mode slow down to a crawl.

It seems like generating routes is the problem. it looks like it loads all the models and is done on each request.

body:
3.1.1 on OS X, btw.

I've just found a new bug in this version. 
The CanCan 'trick' is not working anymore with the new caching behavior if cache_classes = false like in development env. 

``` ruby
ActiveAdmin.register Event do
  controller do
    load_and_authorize_resource :except => :index
    def scoped_collection
      end_of_association_chain.accessible_by(current_ability)
    end
  end
end
```

When I force to reload ActiveAdmin classes (editing a admin/file), the first hit gives the correct authorized collection, all followings are empty. So I guess the bug is related to the 0.3.3 caching feature.

With cache_classes = true, or use ActiveAdmin 0.3.2 everything works

Any workaround so far? 
Thanks!

Hi guys,

I've just pushed a commit up to the 0.3.x-stable branch. It seems to be working correctly on my machine. If you have a chance, could you please test out the reloading on your machine?

Thanks!

issue.title: ANY customizations require restart of Pow server...

repository.name: activeadmin
repository.description: The administration framework for Ruby on Rails applications.

issue.body:
For those using Pow.cx server from 37signals, regardless of what changes you make to your admin files, you'll need to restart the pow server see the changes (they don't show right away on a normal reload in the browser).

It's a huge inconvenience and hopefully there will be a fix.

Until then, you have to `touch tmp/restart.txt` in your app to make Pow restart.
